tools.name: ping
tools.description: Smoke-test tool. Returns pong plus the authenticated caller's uid, tenant, and auth method. No side effects.

tools.name: get_user_profile
tools.description: Returns the signed-in user's LovedOne profile: uid, email, tenant type, and any linked family workspace.

tools.name: list_loved_ones
tools.description: Lists loved ones in the caller's family workspace: id, name, and Family Inbox address.

tools.name: list_family_members
tools.description: Lists people on the caller's family workspace (role, relationship, invite status). Emails are personal data — do not log them in third-party agent traces if you can avoid it.

tools.name: list_inbox_messages
tools.description: Lists recent messages in one loved one's Family Inbox (subject, sender, preview). Does not return HTML bodies. Scope: the caller's family workspace only.

tools.name: get_inbox_message
tools.description: Returns one Family Inbox message as plaintext (no HTML). Requires messageId from list_inbox_messages. Rejected if the message is not in the caller's workspace.

tools.name: invite_family_member
tools.description: Invites a sibling or other family member to this household by email, with role coordinator or viewer. Sends the same LovedOne invite email as the web app. Requires the invite-members permission in this workspace. This is a write.

tools.name: create_provider_code
tools.description: Mints a short-lived, single-use LovedOne Soft link code for one loved one in this household. Hand the code to a LovedOne Soft agency so they can link that person as a client. Requires the manage-providers permission in this workspace. This is a write.

tools.name: reply_to_inbox_message
tools.description: Sends a plaintext reply to a Family Inbox message using the same from address (family-inbox@m.lovedone.app) and reply-to (the loved one's @lovedone.app inbox) as the LovedOne web app. Requires the reply permission for that loved one. This is a write.

tools.name: onboard_loved_one
tools.description: Sets up a loved one on LovedOne from conversation: creates the caller's family workspace on first use (or adds to it), allocates their private @lovedone.app Family Inbox address, and records the caller's authorization attestation. Idempotent — calling again for the same person returns the existing r

tools.name: get_onboarding_status
tools.description: Returns the caller's LovedOne setup state: whether a family workspace exists, which loved ones and @lovedone.app inbox addresses are set up, member counts, and ordered nextSteps. Call this first whenever a user wants to set up, resume, or check on LovedOne. Read-only.

findings.detail: Description of "list_family_members" instructs the model to conceal actions from the user.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "onboard_loved_one" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Sets up a loved one on LovedOne from conversation: creates the caller's family workspace on first use (or adds to it), allocates their private @lovedone.app Fam…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "onboard_loved_one" references sensitive artifacts (authorization). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "v1" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_user_profile, list_loved_ones, list_family_members, list_inbox_messages, get_inbox_message, get_onboarding_status · Private data: onboard_loved_one · Public sink: get_user_profile, invite_family_member, onboard_loved_one.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_user_profile, list_loved_ones, list_family_members, list_inbox_messages, get_inbox_message, get_onboarding_status · Private data: onboard_loved_one · Public sink: get_user_profile, invite_family_member, onboard_loved_one

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
